Synopsis:
The article covers the humanitarian cost impact of an oil price shock triggered by a US-Iran military conflict and subsequent disruption to Strait of Hormuz flows. Oil prices surged above $100/bbl before easing post-ceasefire, but have rebounded above $90 as hostilities resume. Save the Children quantifies $13m in additional aid delivery costs. The piece also flags declining global aid budgets and broader commodity price inflation (food, fertiliser) stemming from the same supply disruption. Near-term uncertainty is elevated by renewed US sanctions rhetoric against Iran.
